string.text: Smart Steward: the autonomous steward failed - see smart_steward.log.
Food you gave no price in the Prices tab uses its average price as the base. Default: on.
Pack animals and riding horses you gave no price use their average price as the base. Default: on.

War horses you gave no price use their average price as the base. When off, they are bought only under the war horse price cap until you type a price. (Noble horses always show their average sell price - they are only ever sold.) Default: off.
Open the Party Steward window when your party enters a town. Default: on.
Open the Party Steward window when your party enters a village. Default: on.

While the full-autonomous steward is on, it never takes your purse below this - both floors above rise to it when they are lower. Raise the price limits to let it spend more freely, never this. Default: 100,000. Range: 0 to 10,000,000.

For when you are rich and done with micromanaging: on arriving at a town or village the steward carries out its plan at once - no window, no questions, no warning - and sums it up in the message log. It never hires in the tavern and never takes your purse below Keep while autonomous. The Party Steward menu entry stays, to look or adjust. When off, the steward only proposes and you click. Default: off.
In a town of your kingdom that is not your clan's, send prisoners to its dungeon for influence instead of gold. Those that do not fit are ransomed. Default: off.

Max buy price of a food = its base price (Prices tab) times this. 2.0 pays up to twice the average - grain at 10 is bought up to 20. Food is cheap and keeps the party alive, so this is generous. Default: 2.0. Range: 0.1 to 10.0.
Count your prisoners when working out the food target - half a man each, as the game feeds them. Default: on.

How many days of food the steward keeps for your party as it will be after the deal - at the game's own rate, perks included (a man eats one food in about 20 days, a prisoner half as much), so 40 days is about 2 food per man. The Instructions tab shows what your days mean per man right now. Default: 40. Range: 1 to 365.
Buy food up to the target and sell what is far above it. Default: on.

The steward starts managing food once your purse holds at least this many denari when you arrive - below it it neither buys nor sells food, and you trade by hand. 0 = always. Default: 2,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
Min sell price of a food = its base price (Prices tab) times this. 0.5 sells surplus food at half the average sell price or better; 0 sells at any price. Default: 0.5. Range: 0.0 to 10.0.
Balanced buys the kinds you hold least of first - every different food lifts morale. Cheapest always buys the cheapest kind. Default: Balanced (variety first).
How far above the target food may pile up before the steward sells: 25 sells only above 125% of the target. Default: 25. Range: 0 to 500.
Max buy price of a horse, mule or camel = its base price (Prices tab) times this. 1.2 pays up to 20% over the average. Richer now? Raise it. Default: 1.2. Range: 0.1 to 10.0.
Min sell price of a horse, mule or camel = its base price (Prices tab) times this. 0.8 sells at 80% of the average sell price or better; 0 sells at any price. Default: 0.8. Range: 0.0 to 10.0.

Off: the steward manages food and horses even when you locked them in the inventory - your locks keep guarding armour and weapons. On: locked food and horses are left alone, like armour and weapons. Default: off.
No purchase takes your purse below this many denari. Default: 1,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
No horse, mule or camel purchase takes your purse below this. Food only answers to the floor above - food comes first. Default: 5,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
Master switch. When off, the steward stays out of the way: no window, no menu entry, no warnings, nothing done on its own. Default: on.
Never pay more than this for a footman's horse, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 500. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Keep horses for the men who walk, so the party moves faster. Default: on.

The steward starts managing riding horses once your purse holds at least this many denari when you arrive - below it it neither buys nor sells them, nor sells noble or lame horses. 0 = always. Default: 5,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
Horses kept for every 100 men on foot: 110 is one each plus 10% spare. The war horses you keep count among them; riding horses fill the rest. Default: 110. Range: 0 to 300.
Never pay more than this for one pack animal, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 300. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Keep a set number of pack animals (sumpter horses, mules, pack camels). Each one carries about 100 more weight. Default: on.
The steward starts managing pack animals once your purse holds at least this many denari when you arrive - below it it neither buys nor sells them. 0 = always. Default: 2,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
How many pack animals the party keeps. Default: 10. Range: 0 to 500.
Open the window by itself only when the steward has something to suggest. Default: on.
Also ransom (or donate) captured lords. A ransomed lord goes free. Default: off.
Offer your prisoners to the town's ransom broker. Default: on.

Sell the party's lame and old horses and pack animals and buy healthy ones in their place. When off they are kept - a lame horse still carries a footman. The steward never buys one either way. Default: on.
Sell food above the target plus the tolerance below, back down to the target, most-held kind first. Default: on.
Offer to sell captured gear in groups (armour, melee weapons, ranged, shields). Default: off.
Include weapons, armour, shields and ammunition in the loot sale. Default: on.
Never sell a piece worth more than this many denari. 0 = no cap. Pieces you locked in the inventory are never sold anyway. Default: 0. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.

Which pieces go first when the market cannot pay for everything: the cheapest (the most weight for the gold), the lowest price per kg, or the most expensive (the game's own habit). Default: Cheapest first.
Sell riding horses above the target, the dearest first. Default: on.

Noble horses are for you and your companions - no troop ever needs one. The steward never buys them and sells the party's noble horses, never below their min sell price in the Prices tab. A noble horse you lock in the inventory is always kept, and a kept one carries a footman. Default: on.
Sell pack animals above the target, the dearest first. Default: on.
Sell war horses above the number to keep, the dearest first. Default: on.
List the mercenary band in the town's tavern. Default: on.
Show the tavern section in towns: wanderers and mercenaries to hire with a click. Default: on.

Show the troops section in towns and villages: the recruits the notables offer you, then your own troops, to recruit or dismiss with a click. Nothing is ever recruited or dismissed unless you click. Default: on.
List the wanderers for hire in the town's tavern. Default: on.
The steward starts keeping war horses once your purse holds at least this many denari when you arrive - below it it neither buys nor sells them. 0 = always. Default: 20,000. Range: 0 to 1,000,000.
Never pay more than this for one war horse, whatever the price book says. 0 = no cap. Not scaled by the buy multiplier. Default: 2,000. Range: 0 to 100,000.
Keep a set number of war horses for upgrading your troops into cavalry. When off, a war horse is just another riding horse to the steward. Default: on.

How many war horses the party keeps - bought up to it, sold above it. They carry footmen until you upgrade men with them (who then ride as cavalry), so they count among the horses per 100 footmen. 0 = none kept: spare war horses are sold. Only once your purse reaches the war horse threshold above. Default: 10. Range: 0 to 500.
Ask before you leave a town or village whose suggestions you never looked at. Default: on.

Horses {HORSES} / {ROOM} before the herd slows you
Your standing orders to the steward. Changes are saved at once - to settings.json, and Mod Options shows them too. Hover a name for what it does.

Final = your base price × the multiplier. An empty box uses the grey average price where auto-fill is on (Instructions tab, Prices). Unticked items are never bought or sold.
Clear your prices - the grey average applies again
Your number - the steward plans around it. Click to hand the row back to the steward.
{FOOTMEN} men on foot · {TOTAL} horses to keep

Dismiss from the lowest tier up: your own troops first, then the men of the types on offer. Shift 5, Ctrl all.
Recruit the highest tier on offer first. Shift 5, Ctrl all.
Show this section's rows. The steward remembers it, even after a restart.
